note: Lines tools/check-repeated-lines.mjs lets a player see whole more than once on the main path (errata 226). Each entry's `why` quotes the ruling that wants the line said again, or says it was found by the check's first run and is waiting for a fix. Adding an entry is loosening the check: record it in proofs/check-friction.json. An entry whose line no longer repeats is reported every run; take it off.

entries.text: I pulled a nugget out of the Feather River the size of a bishop's fist.
entries.why: Doc 03, How it plays: "Thad acquires counters by losing ... and Thad writes it down. This is why Duel One cannot be won"; "A correct counter wins the exchange, and the boast becomes available for Thad to use himself." A boast heard in Duel One comes back in Duel Two by design.

entries.text: I've seen your bishop. He was malnourished.
entries.why: Doc 03, How it plays: "Thad acquires counters by losing. When an opponent uses a boast Thad has no answer to, Thad hears the correct counter from the crowd ... and Thad writes it down." The counter he hears is the counter he then says.

entries.text: My claim assayed at nine hundred dollars to the ton.
entries.why: Doc 03, How it plays: "Thad acquires counters by losing ... This is why Duel One cannot be won." Duel Two is the rematch on the same boasts (doc 03, Duel Two).

entries.text: So did my grandmother, and she was mostly gravel.
entries.why: Doc 03, How it plays: "Thad hears the correct counter from the crowd ... and Thad writes it down." Heard in Duel One, said in Duel Two.

entries.text: I've washed more gold than you've washed shirts.
entries.why: Doc 03, How it plays: "Thad acquires counters by losing ... This is why Duel One cannot be won." Duel Two is the rematch on the same boasts (doc 03, Duel Two).

entries.text: That's true of everyone here, and it's a matter of some concern.
entries.why: Doc 03, How it plays: "Thad hears the correct counter from the crowd ... and Thad writes it down." Heard in Duel One, said in Duel Two.

entries.text: My luck is famous from here to Sacramento.
entries.why: Doc 03, Duel Three: "two returning boasts — Fanshawe deploys pair 4 and pair 9 against Thad, which the player will recognise, because Fanshawe has been listening the whole game."

entries.text: It's famous in Sacramento. That's why you're here.
entries.why: Doc 03, Duel Three: "Fanshawe deploys pair 4 and pair 9 against Thad, which the player will recognise"; How it plays: "Thad hears the correct counter from the crowd ... and Thad writes it down."

entries.text: Every man in this territory owes me money.
entries.why: Doc 03, How it plays: "A correct counter wins the exchange, and the boast becomes available for Thad to use himself"; Duel Three: Fanshawe's "returning boasts ... which the player will recognise, because Fanshawe has been listening the whole game."

entries.text: Every man in this territory owes someone money. You have described the territory.
entries.why: Doc 03, How it plays: "Thad hears the correct counter from the crowd ... and Thad writes it down." Learned from Winnie, said to Fanshawe in Duel Three.

entries.text: 1. A man may not be interrupted in his account.
entries.why: Doc 03, Part One: "a printed handbill of etiquette that Reverend Sowerby reads aloud at unbearable length before every match"; Duel Two: "Then he will enjoy them twice." (He reads all five.)

entries.text: 2. A man's account may be doubted only by a better one.
entries.why: Doc 03, Part One: "a printed handbill of etiquette that Reverend Sowerby reads aloud at unbearable length before every match".

entries.text: 3. Truth is admissible but has never been raised.
entries.why: Doc 03, Part One: "a printed handbill of etiquette that Reverend Sowerby reads aloud at unbearable length before every match".

entries.text: 4. The judges' decision is final, and may be appealed to the same judges.
entries.why: Doc 03, Part One: "a printed handbill of etiquette that Reverend Sowerby reads aloud at unbearable length before every match".

entries.text: 5. No firearms. No knives. No arithmetic.
entries.why: Doc 03, Part One: "a printed handbill of etiquette that Reverend Sowerby reads aloud at unbearable length before every match".

entries.text: Mystery man! Say something quotable. I'll fix it later.
entries.why: Doc 04, FRA_A1: "FRAME (every visit after the first; errata 225, Tyler, 2026-11-09: "proceed")". Seen twice on the main path, both in Act III (C3.2 and C3.7).

entries.text: Have you ever been in the Liar's Assay?
entries.why: Intended (errata 230): Thad asks everyone he meets the same question, the way a newcomer would; each person's answer differs.
